To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the expression of Hox genes is restricted to particular segments of the embryo; (ii) the expression of a Hox-4 gene in the occipital region results in the formation of occipital bones that are transformed towards a more posterior identity, and (iii) this transformation is similar to the posteriorization that occurs when a Hox gene of the HOM-C complex is expressed in a region of the embryo where it is not normally found.
